title: The Null Cabinet
question: Which analyses looked like findings but didn't survive a harder look?

figures.title: The archetype mirage, drawn: real roses against forged ones
figures.deck: The forgery blooms: five specialists at ×2.0–3.0 emerge from pure multinomial noise, and the clustering explains barely more of the real reviewers (35.8%) than of the noise (31.0%).

claims.statement: The clustering explains barely more of the real reviewers (35.8%) than of the noise (31.0%).
claims.derivation: share of between-profile variance the 5-cluster k-means partition explains: 0.3578 (35.8%) for the 98,513 real reviewer profiles, 0.3102 (31.0%) for the synthetic multinomial-noise profiles

claims.statement: Top row: the five clusters k-means (k = 5, seed 7) finds among 98,513 real reviewer-paper profiles (official reviewers, ≥5 units, 2018–2026).
claims.derivation: n_profiles = 98,513 real reviewer-paper profiles (official reviewers with ≥5 units, min_units = 5), clustered k-means with k=5, seed 7

claims.statement: Bottom row: the five clusters the same pipeline finds in synthetic profiles drawn from one shared field mix — profiles that by construction contain no reviewer types at all.
claims.derivation: same k-means (k=5) partition applied to synthetic profiles drawn from one shared multinomial field mix, null seed 46, at each reviewer's own unit volume

claims.statement: The mirage is quantified, not total: the real rows sit 1.15× above the multinomial variance floor at the median standard (1.58× at the most dispersed), and the clustering explains 4.8pp more of the real profiles than of the forged ones, a gap that widens with profile length — a faint true signature, far below what the roses' confidence suggests.

A rose-diagram plate once claimed five reviewer archetypes — Architect, Stress-Tester, Advocate, Gatekeeper, Auditor — from k-means over 98,513 per-reviewer standard profiles, each rose a specialization of ×2.4–3.1 the field. The plate was removed on 2026-08-21.
claims.derivation: each real cluster's own leading (top) standard ratio, ranging from ×2.43 to ×3.1 across the five clusters — the same real[] clusters this appendix's deflating test reruns

claims.statement: The forgery blooms: five specialists at ×2.0–3.0 emerge from pure multinomial noise.
claims.derivation: each synthetic-null cluster's own leading (top) standard ratio, ranging from ×2.03 to ×2.96 across the five clusters — despite the null profiles containing no reviewer types by construction

figures.title: Acceptance rate by breadth of criticism (relocated to the Null Cabinet, 2026-08-25 — expected by construction)
figures.deck: Each additional object criticised comes with about five points less acceptance.

claims.statement: Acceptance falls steeply and then almost linearly — 69% at two objects, 57% at three, then roughly five points for each additional object, down to 27% at nine or more.
claims.derivation: acceptance rate of 2026 decided papers grouped by count of distinct objects criticised (breadth 2, 3, 9-or-more), papers with fewer than 30 at a breadth dropped

claims.statement: The most common paper is criticised on seven of the twelve objects.
claims.derivation: breadth 7 holds the largest paper count (3,459) among the gauntlet buckets

caveats.text: The mirage is quantified, not total: the real rows sit 1.15× above the multinomial variance floor at the median standard (1.58× at the most dispersed), and the clustering explains 4.8pp more of the real profiles than of the forged ones, a gap that widens with profile length — a faint true signature, far below what the roses' confidence suggests.
A median profile holds six units, and at that grain k-means carves sampling noise into confident-looking specialists. This is the test that deleted a plate.

Association only, and here the two quantities are entangled by construction — a weaker paper gives reviewers more to criticise, so breadth of criticism is partly a measurement of the paper rather than a treatment applied to it.
